name: Sunil Sharma

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Sunil Sharma is a poet, fiction writer, editor and academic whose work often begins in the everyday. In a 2015 interview with Geosi Reads, he describes observation as central to his writing and discusses “Mundane, My Muse” as poetry made from ordinary experience. His Piker Press author page records his doctorate in English and his contribution to “Happiness: The Delight-Tree”, placing the poems alongside a wider practice of fiction, criticism and collaborative publishing.

“Aching Voids” gives absence a stubbornly physical life. Broken pavements, shadowed corners and scarred tissue make what is missing feel present, while the short lines repeatedly interrupt the movement of thought. The poem recognises pain as something shared without making every person’s experience interchangeable. Its empty spaces become places where memory can return with unexpected force.
